notes: kb/Work PB5252 landed. §1985:XIII.3.15.3 SR1: "Integer-1 and integer-2 must not exceed three significant digits in length." ReportSectionBinder.ScreenReportLineClauses bounds each LINE NUMBER integer by ReportModel.VerticalLimit (the page limit, at most 999 at 85 by §1985:XIII.3.8.3 SR2) and, below COBOL-2002, by ExceedsThreeSignificantDigits85, the one 999 test the PAGE, LINE NUMBER and NEXT GROUP screens share, so an unpaged report's LINE PLUS 1000 is refused (COBOL2199) while PLUS 0999 (a leading zero is not significant) is accepted. Witnesses: pb5252_line_and_next_group_three_digits (PLUS 0999, runs) and pb5252_line_plus_1000_refused_at_85.

next.reason: 1985: integer-1 and integer-2 'must not exceed three significant digits', no line may fall outside the page subdivision for its group type, and 'Integer-2 may be zero'. §2023:13.18.35.3 SR3: 'Neither integer-1 nor integer-2 shall exceed the page limit, or 9999 if the report is not divided into pages ... Integer-2 may be zero' - the three-digit cap is gone (page limit itself up to 9999, §2023:13.18.39.3 SR5). The subdivision limit stays a syntax rule only for absolute lines and for relative lines ending an absolute group (§2023:13.18.35.3 SR6c, SR6d); a group that cannot fit a page now sets EC-REPORT-PAGE-LIMIT with undefined results (§2023:13.18.35.4 GR2). Looser limits and part of a compile-time refusal moved to a run-time exception condition.
